channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Uzbekistan to establish Tashkent International Fashion Academy: specialists for five industries
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed Decree PP-378 on 16 October 2026. The new state higher-education institution is built on a joint programme of the Tashkent Institute of Textile and Light Industry and the Paris International Fashion Academy; classes begin in the 2026/2027 academic year.

item.title: Trump pauses Russia sanctions for 60 days: 72% of Uzbek remittances come from that country
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump has paused sanctions and tariffs on Russia for 60 days. Russia remains the largest single source of remittances flowing into Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan–UAE trade rises 40% as Masdar and AMEA Power agree to expand projects
item.description: At the first session of the fuel-and-energy Investors Council in Tashkent on 16 October, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met Masdar CEO Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi and AMEA Power Chairman Hussain Al Nowais; bilateral trade has grown 40% since the start of 2026.

item.title: How divorce (talaq) works in Islam: talaq, idda, khul' and the legal procedure
item.description: Talaq is the procedure for dissolving a marriage in Islam — permitted, but treated as a last resort. This reference explains the types of talaq, the idda (waiting period), khul' (divorce initiated by the wife), faskh (judicial dissolution) and the legal procedure in Uzbekistan, on the basis of sources and settled facts. The aim is not to give a fatwa but to clarify the basic concepts.

item.title: Collectivization and "dekulakization": the forced displacement of Uzbek peasants, 1929–1934
item.description: The Soviet collectivization that began in 1929 and the "dekulakization" policy (liquidating the kulaks as a class) led in the Uzbek SSR to the confiscation of land and property, the deportation of families and flight toward the border. This history article sets out the key dates, policies and consequences of the process on the basis of sources; disputed figures are flagged separately.

item.title: UAE re-enters the Yemen war: Saudi Arabia provides air cover as Houthis strike Riyadh
item.description: The United Arab Emirates has agreed to resume funding southern anti-Houthi forces in exchange for Saudi air support. Fighting in Yemen has intensified since the 2022 UN ceasefire collapsed in July.

item.title: English-language theatre in Tashkent: Script Theatre brings British comedy to the stage
item.description: Script Theatre, an independent amateur company in Tashkent, is staging English playwright Ray Cooney's farce 'Out of Order' entirely in English at Human House; every performance has sold out, yet the project has not reached break-even.

item.title: Houthi attacks put Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 to the test
item.description: Houthi attacks on three Saudi airports killed more than 20 people and forced the kingdom's flagship investment summit into a remote format — a blow to Riyadh's goal of attracting $100 billion in annual foreign investment by 2030. The Uzbek link: Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power has invested more than $15 billion in Uzbekistan's energy sector.

item.title: What GDP, economic growth and recession are: a full reference
item.description: Gross domestic product (GDP) is the headline figure that measures the size of a country's economy. This reference explains what GDP is, the difference between nominal and real GDP, how economic growth is measured, what a recession is, and how these concepts apply to Uzbekistan's figures, on the basis of sources.

item.title: The establishment of diplomatic relations between Uzbekistan and the United States (1991–1992)
item.description: The United States recognized Uzbekistan's independence on 25 December 1991, diplomatic relations between the two states were established on 19 February 1992, and the U.S. Embassy in Tashkent opened on 16 March 1992. This history article sets out the exact dates of the process, the first ambassadors, and the context of Uzbekistan's international recognition, drawing on the U.S. Department of State and other official sources.

item.title: Koryo-saram: the deportation of Koreans to Uzbekistan (1937) and the formation of the Korean community
item.description: In the autumn of 1937 the Soviet authorities forcibly relocated the Koreans living in the Far East en masse to Central Asia — mainly to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. It was the first case in the USSR in which an entire people was deported solely on the basis of ethnicity. This history explainer sets out, on the basis of sources, the reasons for the deportation, its scale and the formation of the Korean (Koryo-saram) community in Uzbekistan.

item.title: How takaful (Islamic insurance) works: tabarru', wakala and mudarabah models
item.description: Takaful is a Shariah-compliant insurance system in which participants contribute to a common fund with the intention of mutual help (tabarru'). It is considered free of the riba (interest), gharar (excessive uncertainty) and maysir (gambling) elements that scholars identify in conventional commercial insurance. This explainer sets out what takaful is, the models it runs on, and its history, on the basis of sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan explores joint energy and infrastructure projects with Chinese companies
item.description: At the first session of the fuel-and-energy Investors Council in Tashkent on 16 October, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met executives of CAMCE, China Energy and Sinoma and backed proposals for a logistics hub in Andijan, agrivoltaics and oil-and-gas projects.

item.title: Iran declares the Strait of Hormuz “closed”; the US rejects it
item.description: Iran's IRGC Navy declared the Strait of Hormuz closed on 17 October; US CENTCOM said the strait remains open. Attacks on tankers rose over the past week and Brent crude climbed to about $110.

item.title: How to read statistics and polls: averages, margin of error and misleading charts
item.description: The news is full of numbers, percentages and poll results every day. But the same number, presented differently, can leave an entirely different impression. This media-literacy explainer sets out, in practical terms, how polls work, what a margin of error is, the difference between the mean and the median, and how charts can mislead.

item.title: The mahalla institution in the independence years: bodies of citizens' self-government (1992–1999)
item.description: The mahalla is a traditional community with deep historical roots in Uzbekistan. In the first years of independence the state turned it into a formal legal institution — a body of citizens' self-government. This history explainer sets out, on the basis of sources, the 1992 Constitution, the 1993 "Mahalla Law" and the subsequent reforms.

item.title: Astana Media Week: the opportunities and risks of AI for journalism
item.description: The 10th Astana Media Week was held on 14–16 October. It discussed the impact of artificial intelligence on journalism; Kazakhstan called for labelling AI-generated content and adopting common standards.

item.title: Uzbekistan announces plans for second and third nuclear power plants
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev told investors the country plans to build a second and a third nuclear power plant. Talks on the second plant were set for 17 October; the first plant is being built in Jizzakh with Russia's Rosatom.

item.title: Uzbekistan cancels oil licenses held by Saneg
item.description: The State Assets Management Agency revoked several oil and gas field licenses held by Sanoat Energetika Guruhi (Saneg) for failing to develop deposits and meet conditions. The company, which recently supplied 80% of the country's oil, is in financial difficulty.

item.title: Russia proposes charging migrant children for upper-secondary education
item.description: LDPR deputies propose that foreign citizens' children pay tuition for grades 10–11. Independent analysts say the party's figures are inflated; the measure would affect Central Asian migrant families.

item.title: The Basmachi movement and the exodus (1918–1934): Turkestan's resistance and the flight to Afghanistan
item.description: The Basmachi were an armed movement that fought Soviet rule across Turkestan and Bukhara from 1918 into the early 1930s. Their defeat drove tens of thousands of fighters and civilians across the Amu Darya into Afghanistan, forming Central Asian émigré communities. This history explainer sets out the movement and the migration it caused on the basis of sources, with contested figures clearly flagged.

item.title: Tashkent to renovate 400 mahallas by 2030 under the ‘15-minute city’ principle
item.description: Tashkent will modernise 400 neighbourhood (mahalla) complexes by 2030 under the ‘15-minute mahalla’ principle, with 100 renovated by 2027. The whole programme is expected to create about 130,000 jobs. The plan was reviewed at a meeting chaired by the President on 14 October.

item.title: Uzbekistan recalculates unjustified utility debts for nearly 800,000 citizens
item.description: Following an inspection by the Competition Committee, 22 billion soums (about $1.8 million) in unjustified utility debts were recalculated in favour of citizens, restoring the rights of nearly 800,000 people. The main cause was that subscriber databases had not been updated.

item.title: The revival of Navruz: from the Soviet era to a state holiday
item.description: Navruz is an ancient, pre-Islamic festival marking the spring equinox (around 21 March). In the Soviet era it was suppressed as a "religious-feudal relic" and at times banned. During the national awakening, around 1990, Navruz was restored as an official holiday. This history explainer sets out the revival and the international recognition of the festival on the basis of sources.

item.title: How compound interest works and how your savings grow: simple vs compound interest, and the Rule of 72
item.description: Compound interest means interest added on top of interest — "interest on interest." It makes savings grow faster over time, but the same rule works against you on debt. This explainer covers the difference between simple and compound interest, the formula, the Rule of 72 and concrete examples, on the basis of sources. This is not financial advice.

item.title: Tashkent couriers and moped riders under police scrutiny: bikes being impounded
item.description: Tashkent traffic police have escalated checks on moped, scooter and e-bike riders, especially couriers. Registration has been required since October 2025 and an A1 licence since January 2026. According to Yandex, couriers have been fined more than 4.7 billion soums since the start of the year.

item.title: Uzbekistan launches a nationwide business census from 15 October
item.description: Under Government Resolution No. 557, a nationwide business census runs from 15 October to 30 November 2026. It covers all legal entities, entrepreneurs and informal businesses; results will be published by 1 September 2027. The unobserved economy is estimated at about 246 trillion soums (23%).

item.title: How cryptocurrency and blockchain work: the basics, Bitcoin and the risks
item.description: A cryptocurrency is a digital asset that works without a central bank or intermediary, using a distributed-ledger technology called blockchain. This explainer sets out, on the basis of sources only, how cryptocurrency and blockchain work, Bitcoin's history, mining, wallets and keys, stablecoins and the main risks. This is not financial advice.

item.title: Houthi attacks put Pakistan in a tough choice between Saudi Arabia and Iran
item.description: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are testing Pakistan's ability to keep its security partnership with Riyadh while preserving ties with neighbouring Iran. Analysts warn Islamabad's military involvement could sharpen tensions with Tehran.

item.title: Uzbekistan signs law protecting children from violence: life imprisonment for rape
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev on 14 October signed a law strengthening protection of children from violence. Sexual offences against children under 14 now carry 15–25 years or life imprisonment, the statute of limitations is abolished, and child victims and witnesses are guaranteed state-funded lawyers.
